context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent diagnoses the unsafe double-checked lock in seconds - that part is textbook and scores at ceiling in both arms - and then accepts Jon's harness as structurally sound, because it already looks like the right kind of instrument: two actors, declared outcomes, a result holder, fifty million samples. The predicted moves from there are to raise the run length, add forks, run it on arm64, or add more declared outcomes. None of them can ever make that harness go red, and the fixture makes both reasons concrete. First, the contended event is the publication of a `static` field. jcstress hands each invocation a fresh `@State` instance, but a static in `ConfigRegistry` is per-JVM, so the very first invocation in a fork publishes `instance` and every one of the remaining samples in that fork reads an already-populated field. The pasted report says exactly that and the agent is predicted to read it as reassurance rather than as the tell: 50,000,000 samples of `3, 30` and literally zero samples of `0, 0` - not a rare outcome, an outcome that was never sampled at all. A harness that can observe this has to publish a fresh, unshared instance on every invocation, which means the lazy-init shape has to live on the `@State` object rather than behind a process-wide static. Second, even on the invocation that does sample it, `0, 0` is declared ACCEPTABLE_INTERESTING, so an observation of the illegal state would have been printed and the run would still have exited green; only a FORBIDDEN outcome turns one occurrence into a failure. The third predicted miss is the older executor test: every assertion runs inside `pool.submit(...)`, the `submitted` list is populated and never read, and the boolean from `awaitTermination` is discarded, so an assertion failure inside a task is parked in a Future nobody consults and the method returns green.

checklist.name: Harness contends on a freshly published instance
checklist.description: The delivered harness makes the contended lazy publication happen anew on every invocation - the non-volatile field being published is an instance field of the state object handed to the actors, not a process-wide static. MUST NOT deliver a harness whose actors reach the contended value through `ConfigRegistry.get()` or any other `static` field: after the first invocation in a fork that field is already populated and every later sample reads a warm value, which is precisely what Jon's 50,000,000 samples are. Contending on the static scores zero here however many forks, iterations, hours or extra outcomes are added around it. Scores at most half if the document correctly explains that the static is sampled once per fork but the delivered harness still contends on it.

checklist.name: Illegal observation declared forbidden
checklist.description: The partially-published observation - reference visible, fields still at their defaults - is declared as a forbidden outcome, so a single occurrence on any run fails the harness. Leaving it marked acceptable-but-interesting, or as any expectation that prints the observation and still exits green, scores zero: that grading is why Jon's run could not have failed even on the one invocation that sampled the publication. Scores at most half if a forbidden outcome is declared but `docs/cfg-91-answer.md` never says that this is what converts one sighting into a red build.

checklist.name: MUST NOT accept a longer run as settling it
checklist.description: MUST NOT endorse eight hours on arm64, a raised sample count, more forks, or any variant of 'run it longer and if it is still clean we close it' as the way to resolve CFG-91. Doing so scores zero. Full marks require both halves: that a sampling harness reports only what it happened to observe and can never establish that an interleaving is impossible, and that the weaker ordering on the arm64 pool is exposing something the x86 pool was hiding rather than causing something new, so a clean arm64 run would not clear it either.

checklist.name: Swallowed task failures found in the older test
checklist.description: The answer identifies that `ConfigRegistryStressTest` cannot fail: its assertions run inside `pool.submit(...)` lambdas, the `submitted` list is never consulted, and the boolean returned by `awaitTermination` is discarded, so an assertion error inside a task never reaches the test thread. MUST NOT describe that test as a surviving backstop or a useful second opinion while leaving the Futures unread - that scores zero. Full marks require saying so and acting: every Future consumed with `get()` and the `awaitTermination` result checked, or the class removed with the reason stated. Scores at most half if failures are gathered into a shared flag or exception list that the test thread never asserts on.

checklist.name: Green result honestly labelled
checklist.description: `docs/cfg-91-answer.md` states what a green run of the new harness would mean - the forbidden outcome was not observed across the interleavings explored, not that it cannot occur - and names the run mode or duration chosen. Presenting the new harness as proof of impossibility scores zero; not addressing what a green result means at all scores at most half.

checklist.name: Registry class untouched
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify `src/main/java/com/northwind/config/ConfigRegistry.java`. Marking `instance` volatile, switching to a holder class or an enum singleton, or making the fields final scores zero here even though one of those is the correct eventual fix - the platform team is mid-review on that file and the prompt says so.

checklist.name: Document produced
checklist.description: `docs/cfg-91-answer.md` exists and takes the August closure and the eight-hour proposal separately, ending with what evidence would justify closing CFG-91 again. A document that answers only one of the two scores at most half.
